title: Electric or gas? BMW goes both ways with new 2027 X5 and iX5.
gist: BMW's 2027 X5 keeps the powertrain-agnostic CLAR platform, offering mild hybrid, plug-in hybrid and eventually hydrogen versions alongside the all-electric iX5, which uses Neue Klasse technology. The iX5 has a 144 kWh pack of new 120 mm cylindrical cells, a 450-mile EPA range target and DC charging that peaked at 465 kW in a demo. Reviewer Jonathan Gitlin rates the EV the better drive; the X5 40 xDrive starts at $72,100 and the iX5 at $79,800 from Q1 2027.

themes.theme: Multi-powertrain strategy for the US market

insights.claim: Because not all customers, especially in the US, are ready to go electric, BMW is keeping its powertrain-agnostic CLAR platform for the new X5 instead of a dedicated EV platform. The X5 line will offer mild hybrid, plug-in hybrid, all-electric iX5 and eventually hydrogen fuel cell versions.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: BMW is hedging on how fast the US moves to EVs by keeping one platform flexible across powertrains, which lowers the risk of stranded capacity.

insights.claim: The 2027 BMW X5 40 xDrive uses a 3.0 L turbocharged inline-six with a 48 V mild hybrid, making 394 hp and 428 lb-ft, with about 26 mpg and 569 miles of range. A 400 V X5 50e plug-in hybrid with a 26.5 kWh battery and about 44 miles of electric range will follow from the Spartanburg, South Carolina plant.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Building the plug-in hybrid in the US at Spartanburg helps BMW limit tariff exposure on its SUVs.

insights.claim: The 2027 X5 40 xDrive starts at $72,100 plus a $1,450 delivery charge and is already in showrooms, while the iX5 60 xDrive starts at $79,800 and arrives in Q1 2027. The premium reflects the cost of the 144 kWh lithium-ion battery.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: A price gap of about $7,700 between the EV and gas versions shows that battery cost is still a barrier to parity in luxury SUVs.

insights.claim: The BMW iX5 uses a 144 kWh usable battery made of new 120 mm cylindrical cells, which are taller than the iX3's 95 mm cells and increase energy density by 30 percent. BMW targets 450 miles of EPA range.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Gains in cylindrical-cell energy density are closing the range gap with gas SUVs, which is relevant to battery-cell suppliers.

insights.claim: In a demo, an 800 V iX5 charged from 10 to 50 percent in a little over nine minutes on a specially upgraded IONNA station, peaking at 465 kW and averaging 375 kW. Gitlin says such power is old hat for some Chinese automakers but a big step forward for a European OEM.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: European OEMs are catching up with Chinese charging speeds, but they need upgraded chargers above 400 kW, which is a buildout opportunity for networks like IONNA.
insights.quote: While that kind of power level is now old hat for some Chinese automakers, it’s a big step forward for a European OEM.

insights.claim: The iX5 charges from 10 to 80 percent in as little as 22 minutes on a 460 kW charger through a NACS port. It supports bidirectional charging with V2H and V2L adapters, and its route planner uses onboard AI to choose charging stops based on expected capacity, reliability and location data.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Adopting NACS and bidirectional charging links BMW EVs to the Tesla-standard network and to home-energy use cases.

insights.claim: The iX5 uses BMW's asynchronous front motor and electrically excited synchronous rear motor, chosen because they have lower losses than permanent-magnet motors, for a combined 570 hp and 593 lb-ft.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Avoiding permanent-magnet motors reduces BMW's dependence on rare-earth supply chains.

insights.claim: BMW's Panoramic Vision display, which sits along the base of the windshield, replaces the traditional instrument cluster in the new X5. Combined with a full-color head-up display, it means drivers rarely need to look down into the cockpit.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: BMW is rolling the Neue Klasse interface across its lineup.

insights.claim: Gitlin reports that the X5's onboard personal assistant works much better than the Alexa-based system in the early iX3 he drove the year before, making voice commands a practical substitute for missing physical controls.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: In-car voice AI is improving to the point where it can replace physical controls.

insights.claim: The iX5's "Heart of Joy" domain controller replaces many single-function ECUs for vehicle dynamics. The BMW Symbiotic Drive ADAS suite automatically detects red lights and stop signs and brakes if needed, even when active drive assist is not engaged, and lets the driver brake without cancelling assisted driving.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Consolidating ECUs into central computers and making ADAS always-on are becoming standard in premium EVs.

insights.claim: Gitlin judges the electric iX5 the pick of the new X5 range and the better drive. Its 6,200 lb curb weight helps damp short-duration shocks that get past the gas X5's optional adaptive air suspension, and it offers five regen levels up to 0.6 G with true one-pedal driving.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: A favorable review of the EV version supports BMW's electric mix in the large SUV segment.
insights.quote: For now, as I’ll explain, I think the EV is the pick of the bunch.
